Azariah begat Seraiah--</hi>He filled the supreme pontifical office at the destruction of Jerusalem, and, along with his deputy and others, he was executed by Nebuchadnezzar's orders at Riblah (<reference osisRef="2Kgs.25.18">2Ki 25:18</reference>, <reference osisRef="2Kgs.25.21">21</reference>). The sons of Levi; Gershom, &c.--</hi>This repetition (see <reference osisRef="1Chr.6.1">1Ch 6:1</reference>) is made, as the historian here begins to trace the genealogy of the Levitical families who were not priests. entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3692"/><div sID="gen5283" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3692"/><hi type="bold">67-81. they gave unto them of the cities of refuge--</hi>The names of the cities given here are considerably different from those applied to them (<reference osisRef="Josh.21.13-Josh.21.19">Jos 21:13-19</reference>). In the lapse of centuries, and from the revolutions of society, changes might have been expected to take place in the form or dialectic pronunciation of the names of those cities; and this will sufficiently account for the variations that are found in the lists as enumerated here and in an earlier book. As to these cities themselves that were assigned to the Levites, they were widely remote and separated--partly in fulfilment of Jacob's prophecy (<reference osisRef="Gen.49.7">Ge 49:7</reference>), and partly that the various districts of the country might obtain a competent supply of teachers who might instruct the people in the knowledge, and animate them to the observance, of a law which had so important a bearing on the promotion both of their private happiness and their national prosperity. <chapter eID="1Chr.6"/>
